newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian states agree to scrap bank FID tax.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian states agree to scrap bank FID tax.

text.p: A meeting of Australian premiers and chief ministers agreed on Friday to abolish the financial institution duty (FID) on bank transaction, with the exception of the state of Queensland.
"This is without a doubt the most signficiant reform of state taxes in 15 years," said Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett told reporters after the meeting.
Queensland does not have a FID tax. Kennett said the FID would be replaced with what he called a reformed debit tax on a national basis if Queensland agreed to participate in this.

"Premiers and chief ministers with the exception of queensland have agreed to abolish financial institution duties and replace it with a reformed debit tax on a national basis if Queensland participates," a communique issued by the committee said.
Queensland premier Rob Borbidge suggested that the initiative was conditional on Queensland's participation.
"It would be difficult for it to proceed without Queensland's involvement," he told Reuters.
The proposed new debits tax would effectively combine the two state charges on bank transactions.
"This would look at combining the FID and BAD in one tax and it would put in a rate of up 0.1 percent," Kennett said.
"So you are talking about 10 cents in A$100 transactions in moneys moving out of accounts," he said.
The communique said the move would cut the tax burden on low income households and small businesses.
